messages:
maya: heads up — after last night's idp cert rotation we started seeing session bounces for some EU users, and a handful of SCIM provisioning jobs dropped roles. anyone else seeing this?

sam: seeing the same. users hit SSO, get redirected back with login success but session cookie cleared immediately. repro on Chrome and Firefox for me. :thinking_face:

jen: I noticed SCIM logs show 200 for user patch, but our audit index doesn't show the role change event. looks like our service accepted the SCIM payload but the role write failed downstream.

maya: @sam can you paste the SP logs? also @aaron did KMS rekey run last night? could be decrypt failures when writing encrypted extId.

sam: pasted minimal trace: 
```
[sp] 2026-03-22T02:13:45Z Received SAMLResponse size=5.8kb
[sp] 2026-03-22T02:13:45Z Assertion signature verified with cert-thumb: ab:cd:ef:33
[sp] 2026-03-22T02:13:45Z Created session id=sess_9f8a token=*** cookie set
[sp] 2026-03-22T02:13:45Z Session validate: upstream KMS decrypt failed: rpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
[sp] 2026-03-22T02:13:45Z Cleared session id= sess_9f8a
```

jen: that KMS error line is the smoking gun for role-propagation drop. our provisioning path decrypts extid before role mapping. if decrypt times out we swallow and ack SCIM to avoid retry storms.

aaron: I ran the rekey at 02:10 UTC and the new key was promoted at 02:11. Control plane reported zero errors. KMS metrics show a short spike in latency 02:11–02:14 (p95->3.4s). Might have overlapped with active sessions.

maya: ok — so likely race between rekey & active decrypts. but why did SAML assertion verify ok against rotated cert? certs updated in IdP metadata at 02:05. SP picks up new cert. cookie creation still needs decrypt of existing server-side blob.

sam: reproducible locally by forcing KMS to sleep 3s on decrypts — session gets created then immediately invalidated. workaround is to fallback to cached decrypted extid when KMS times out, but that carries risk if key actually changed.

jen: for SCIM: we currently ack PATCH even on decrypt failure to avoid duplicates from idp. maybe switch to 409/retry-once if decrypt fails? that will surface backpressure to the IdP.

aaron: I can add a short re-enqueue: on KMS timeout try cached key decrypt (if cache within 24h) else surface 409. low risk and buys time during rotations.

maya: agree. also need audit coverage — right now failed role writes leave no audit event. add an audit entry before attempting write: "attempted role write (pending)" then update to success/failure. that way we can trace.

jen: +1. I'll add an audit preflight. also create a prometheus counter for scim_role_write_failures_kms_timeout.

sam: quick triage actions: 1) revert aggressive ack behavior for SCIM, 2) add preflight audit event, 3) implement cached-decrypt fallback with a strict TTL, 4) postmortem note for rotations. anyone want to own rollout?

aaron: I can own 3 and 1. will open PRs today and target canary to eu-prod first.

maya: I'll own 2 and the postmortem writeup. will include timeline + KMS latency graphs.

oncall-bot: incident created — INC-2026-031-07: "IdP cert rotation caused KMS decrypt latency -> session invalidation & SCIM role drops". Paging oncall.

sam: also a vuln triage note — our design swallows KMS timeout in a few places to keep IdP happy. that's a principle risk: silent data loss. postmortem should propose a pattern: either explicit retry with backoff OR fail-fast to surface to IdP.

jen: noted for postmortem. I'll draft recommended pattern.

maya: thanks team. action items tracked in the incident ticket. tagging infra to review KMS rekey timing window (we should coordinate rotations with low traffic windows). :thumbsup:
